about: Which links in a conversation become Orbit cards, and where the card goes — one set of cases
both clients are proved against. OrbitKit's `OrbitLinkTests` reads it on Linux; the web's
vitest reads the same file, so the two ends cannot drift into two sets of rules.
Each case: `text` (the message, as markdown), an optional `host` (the server the reader is
signed in to; the file's own `host` when absent), and `blocks` — the rendered blocks the text
must become, in order. A block is either a card or a markdown block:
{"card": {"kind": "task|session|project|list|wiki", "id": "<canonical uuid>",
"url": "<the page URL as written>"}}      — from a pasted page URL
{"card": {"kind": "...", "id": "<canonical uuid>", "ref": "orbit-task:<publicId>"}}
— from an agent's reference
{"markdown": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "..."}}
{"markdown": {"type": "heading", "level": 2, "text": "..."}}
{"markdown": {"type": "list", "items": [{"indent": 0, "ordered": false,
"number": null, "text": "...", "checkbox": null}]}}
{"markdown": {"type": "quote", "text": "..."}}
{"markdown": {"type": "code", "language": "bash", "code": "..."}}
{"markdown": {"type": "table", "headers": [...], "rows": [[...]],
"alignments": ["none|left|center|right"]}}
{"markdown": {"type": "image", "source": "...", "alt": "..."}}
{"markdown": {"type": "rule"}}
A card's `id` is the CANONICAL spelling — a lowercase UUID — whichever spelling the link used:
comparing what was written instead of the object it names is the silent miss this whole rule
exists to prevent. `url` / `ref` keeps what was written verbatim, because that is what the card
replaced and what Copy link hands back.
A wiki entry is the one kind with no page URL of its own: its page is `/wiki/<space>/e/<id>` — a
space AND an entry — while the id a link carries names only the entry. So `orbit-wiki:<id>` is the
whole of how an entry is referenced, and a `/wiki/…` URL a person pastes stays the URL it is.
The ids are production rows from 2026-09-23 (the same conversation the iOS mock is drawn from),
except the two wiki entries, which are from the note those same sessions were handed.

cases.name: url at the start of a line, words after it
url alone on its line
url at the end of a line, words before it
url in the middle of a sentence
the same object written as a UUID, upper case — one object, one id
two links in one message, two cards
a query string and a fragment are not part of which object it names
a sentence's full stop after a url is not part of it
the pre-1.0 session paths, which are sessions too
…and the agent-scoped spelling of the same path
a host with a port, which is how a local deployment is reached
another port on the same host is another server
another site's link, whatever its path says
excluded: an api path — the shape of a pasted error log
excluded: a download path
excluded: the install page
excluded: a share link, which is somebody else's session by design
excluded: /lists/none names no list
excluded: any other page of the deployment
a markdown link with a label keeps its label, even to this deployment
a url inside a code span is code, not a link
a url in a list item stays where it is
a url in a quote stays where it is
a url in a heading stays where it is
an agent's reference alone in a paragraph is a card
…and a project reference, and a list reference, and a session one
a reference written into a sentence stays the name link it is today
